title: Appaquogue
summary: Appaquogue, also written Apoquogue, is identified as an East Hampton placename for a farming district near a flaggy meadow. The same source notes that the vicinity was locally called Lily Pond. It is kept separate from Apocock in Westhampton because the sources describe different places, even though the names share a related meaning.
map_geometry_source: Existing point retained for the Lily Pond vicinity identified with Appaquogue; location is approximate/general.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Montaukett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Appaquogue preserves an East Hampton placename tied to a flaggy meadow near the Lily Pond area, where useful wetland plants were part of the local landscape. Its interpretation as a place where flags grow points to Native ecological knowledge and to materials used in mats, coverings, and everyday life. The name links language, plants, water, and community use in one remembered place.
history_content: Appaquogue was known in East Hampton township, though no early town source has been tied to the available references yet. The placename is best understood here through local usage and language history rather than as a boundary-specific land description.
translation_content:
The recorded form Apoquogue appears in the sources. J. Hammond Trumbull interprets Appaquogue as a place where flags grow or a lodge-covering place. The interpretation points to cat-tail flags and other plant materials used for mats and coverings.

Why Place Names Matter

“The origin of other names which seem inappropriate or absurd is explained when the history of the name is known.”

— Isaac Taylor, Names and Their Histories (1896), Internet Archive scan leaf 19
whereintheworld_content: Appaquogue connects the Lily Pond area with Native place naming, wetland plants, and everyday materials used in housing and community life. It also helps distinguish related Algonquian names that share roots but belong to different Long Island places.
